newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - NOV 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - NOV 19.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--The Bank of Greece will attempt to avert the dangers of speculative capital inflows by frequent and visible fluctuations of the drachma's parity in 1997 as well as avoiding setting a target for the parity. The central bank's only goal will be inflation and credit expansion.

--The continuing dependence of the Greek economy on agriculture and the small number and character of Greek businesses are two of the major structural obstacles to the government's efforts to European convergence, according to a Reuters review.

--Greece's telecommunications organisation OTE will announce its new manager in the coming days, following approval from prime minister and ministries. Rumours point to a manager of Greek descent working with a major organisation 'across the Atlantic'. He/she will get an annual fee of around 100 million drachmas.
--Forty inspection teams from the international houses of Peat Marwick, Ernst & Young and Deloitte & Touche begin checks of all brokerage firms today to give a clearer picture of their status.
--Olympic Catering last week signed a five-year contract with Hochtief for the privison of food services to workers building the new Athens international airport at Spata.
IMERISIA

--Banks react to Prime Minister Costas Simitis's announcement yesterday that the government plans to tax interest on interbank deposits. Bankers say that they have already been targeted enough by plans to increase taxation and the taxation of state titles.
--Simitis appears to have succeeded in convincing his PASOK MPs and Central Committee members to unite in support of the government's economic policy, following a 10-hour meeting yesterday.
--1996 will end with a 300 billion 'black hole' and a public deficit of an estimated 35 trillion, up from 31.9 trillion at end-1995, according to a finance ministry report.
KERDOS

--Simitis stresses that a failure of the government's economic plans will hurt the lower classes. He calls for "sacrifices with hope" for the coming years, in an effort to get Greece to participate in European economic and monetary union (EMU).
--Local government will consider increasing municipal taxes by up to as much as 47 percent.
--The only certainty for EMU is Luxembourg, while Greece appears to be the favourite to be left out, according to a European-wide survey of leading economists and bankers by Reuters.
EXPRESS
--Intense interest noted in bid to be one of three natural gas distribution companies in Attica, Thessaloniki and Thessaly. The competition will be announced in March or April 1997.
--The State Audit Council's report for fiscal year 1995 shows expenses exceeeding inflows and lending needs exceeded forecast targets by 130 percent.
--The European Commission is to ask the Greek agriculture ministry to return 77.5 million Ecu, mistakenly granted in 1992.
NAFTEMBORIKI

--The bourse's depository and guarantee fund will cover the 2.6 billion drachma default by Delta Securities today, as the president of the capital market commission meets with a committee of brokers to decide on a temporary limit on transactions for firms, in accordance with their share capital.

--The electronic transaction network linking the central bank with other commercial and state-run banks - which is still at the experimental stage - will lead to radical changes in the secondary titles market.
--Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
